stories.event: The 27 EU leaders hold an informal meeting in Dublin on Friday 13 November 2026, the day after the European Political Community summit there; European Council President António Costa made artificial intelligence the headline topic, with Mistral AI chief Arthur Mensch and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton invited, and aims to finish by 16:00. After Italian PM Giorgia Meloni complained on 5 Nov of European 'disarray' in Ukraine diplomacy, Costa agreed to make time for a debate on who speaks for the EU in the peace talks; an EU source told EUobserver that Dublin will be an initial debate on the 'profile, format and mandate' of a possible EU envoy, with names left to the December summit. Zelensky has urged the EU to settle it by the end of November, and US envoy Jared Kushner urged Europe to coordinate. Leaders also discuss Ukraine's 2027 financing, where the EU has pledged €45bn of a roughly €70bn gap and Germany wants all states to share the burden, and the next long-term budget. The successor to ECB President Christine Lagarde is due to be appointed at the 17–18 December summit, not in Dublin. Czech angle (merged from the planned story cz-babis-dublin): Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš flew from Prague-Kbely to Dublin on 11 November 2026 for the European Political Community summit (12 Nov) and the informal meeting of EU leaders (13 Nov). In a letter to European Council President António Costa published on 10 Nov he rejected linking further Ukraine financing with talks on the EU's long-term budget, and backed Giorgia Meloni's call for the EU to decide by end-December who negotiates for it on Ukraine, with a 'clear and strong political mandate'. On 10 Nov in Bratislava he and Slovak PM Robert Fico rejected German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's call for all EU states to help cover Ukraine's 2027 budget gap; Babiš did not say clearly whether Czechia would join a further loan, while Fico ruled it out and proposed Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič, or possibly Czech President Petr Pavel, as EU negotiator. Before leaving, Babiš said Czechia wants a 'substantially higher' share in the second round of the EU's SAFE defence loans than the €2.06bn it took in the first. The EU has pledged €45bn of Ukraine's roughly €70bn gap for 2027 without agreeing how to raise it.

Maritime monitors counted 37 ships attacked in October, the most of the war, and UKMTO-reported incidents fell on 10 of the last 14 Gulf days. stories.event: The Czech Chamber of Deputies holds an extraordinary sitting (its 36th) from 09:00 on Friday 13 November 2026 with a single item: the second reading of the government bill introducing an extraordinary tax on refineries (sněmovní tisk 311). The tax, 50% of the increase in refining margins over 2025 for 2026 and 2027, would in practice hit only Orlen Unipetrol's Kralupy and Litvínov plants and is expected to raise about CZK 5.5bn for 2026. The bill cleared its first reading on 13 October after the opposition failed to have it rejected or returned to the government. On 11 November the budget committee backed it without amendments and rejected STAN's proposals. TOP 09 will propose cutting the rate to 39.5%, the Pirates to 25% with an extension to coal power producers. Prime Minister Andrej Babiš, who is in Dublin on Friday, said on 11 November he does not expect sector levies to come up in the Chamber this week, and Industry Minister Karel Havlíček said the government is not considering them now.

stories.event: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the Producer Price Index for October 2026 at 08:30 ET (14:30 CET) on Friday 13 November, a date set in its September release. In September final-demand producer prices jumped 1.3% from August, the largest rise since March 2022, driven by a 10.8% surge in energy prices; the 12-month rate reached 6.3%. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect a 0.4% rise in October and 0.3% excluding food and energy, but that survey predates the October consumer-price data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% expected, with energy up 0.7% after 5.2% in September. In six recent months the first PPI print missed the consensus by 0.53 points on average (root mean square), with large upside misses in April and September.

stories.event: On 5 Nov 2026 the Czech National Bank's Bank Board raised the two-week repo rate by 0.25 pp to 4.00%, with the discount rate at 3.00% and the Lombard rate at 5.00%, effective 6 Nov. The vote was 4–3, the narrowest possible majority; the three in the minority voted to keep rates unchanged, but their names were not given. Governor Aleš Michl called the move fine-tuning, not the start of a new tightening cycle, and said the hold side argued that rising government bond yields were already doing part of the work. The ČNB's publication schedule lists the written record of the meeting, which names how each member voted, and the autumn Monetary Policy Report for Friday 13 Nov. In June, Karina Kubelková was the only member to vote against a hike. Ahead of the meeting, Deputy Governor Jan Frait told Bloomberg the case for a hike was relatively strong but waiting a little longer was not a big risk.

stories.event: Ten days after the 3 Nov election, Mississippi counties must submit certified results of the US Senate race by Friday 13 Nov; the state certifies by 3 Dec and Mississippi has no recount mechanism. Democrat Scott Colom led Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 3,176 votes (470,309 to 467,133, 49.11% to 48.79%) with 98% counted as of 11 Nov, up from 1,882 on 5 Nov. Affidavit (provisional) ballots, many caused by the state's Experian-based roll purge, have broken for Colom; Hinds County, the largest and heavily Democratic, accepted 817 and rejected 1,609 affidavits and was scanning them on 11 Nov. AP had not called the race as of 11 Nov. Hyde-Smith said on 10 Nov she still expected to win, and her lawyers demanded counties segregate affidavit ballots. Senate control does not depend on the race: Democrats hold at least 54 seats. Colom would be the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Mississippi since 1982 and its first Black senator since Reconstruction.

stories.event: The UN Security Council must renew the Yemen 2140 sanctions regime (asset freeze and travel ban) before it expires on 14 November 2026, a Saturday, together with the Panel of Experts' mandate, which runs to 15 December; the UK is the penholder and the exact vote day had not been announced by 11 November. France, the UK and the US want wider sanctions, maritime interdiction and scrutiny of Iran's support, while Russia and China argue that expansion would escalate tensions, and China has attacked the panel's reports naming it as a source of dual-use goods. The question is whether the Council renews the regime unanimously or splits again.

stories.event: Statistics Poland (GUS) is due to publish its flash estimate of third-quarter 2026 GDP on Friday 13 November, according to ING; GUS releases its signal publications at 09:30. Growth in the second quarter, first put at 3.8% year on year, has since been revised to 4.1%, and the comparison quarter, July–September 2025, now stands at a strong 4.0%. ING expects growth to have slowed to 3.4%, as higher fuel prices weighed on consumption and net exports turned negative, while investment stayed buoyant. mBank has warned that weak construction may pull the third quarter down. Banks expect growth of about 3.7% for the whole of 2026.

story.event: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass on the Pampas de Pimentel esplanade near Chiclayo, Peru, at 10:30 local time on Friday 13 November, his first Mass of the Peru leg (11–16 Nov) of a Latin American tour that began in Uruguay and Argentina. Chiclayo is the diocese he led as bishop from 2015 to 2023. Lambayeque's regional governor Jorge Pérez says close to one million faithful are expected; about 150,000 people registered for tickets in the first hours, and the site opens at 20:00 the evening before. In Buenos Aires on 9 Nov the Vatican estimated more than 2.5 million people at his Mass, the largest of his pontificate. After the Mass he meets clergy and the university community; he goes on to Cusco and Pucallpa on 15 Nov and ends with a Mass in Lima on 16 Nov.
